2026 Season 18 reports

🦆 LPCC Duck Report — 13-19 August 2026 🥇

9 ducks
Week 18 · 13 Aug 2026 – 19 Aug 2026
A properly productive week for the exclusive zero club: nine ducks laid across eight fixtures, seven of them on Saturday alone. Let's tour the grounds. Saturday 15 August 1st XI v Mersham Sports CC (h) Jordan Austin opened both the innings and the day's misery, ct Katie Jordan b Ashley Cook for his 3rd of the season and 53rd career duck — 14th on the all-time list, with Duck of the Year 2021 and Diamond Duck honours already banked. On this very day in 1964, John Thirkell (1943-1977, 90 ducks, five-time Duck of the Year) was also dismissed for nought, so Jordan keeps fine calendar company. Will Hughes (b Anurag Mhatre) brought up his 7th career duck, drawing level with current campaigner Daniel Baker on the same tally. A paid-up Debutante Duck club member from his actual debut, long since filed away. Thomas Beeney (b James Rand) notched a 9th duck of the season — 58th career, 10th all-time — and with a Duck of the Year 2026 board entry already secured, he isn't just topping this season's charts, he's defending the crown in real time. 2nd XI v Tonbridge CC (a) Aaron Hughes, ct Prendergast b Batley off just 3 balls, opens his season account and moves to 21 career ducks, level with Dave Todd (1978-2014). Tidy symmetry: his kin Will Hughes was also walking back for nought the very same Saturday, one XI over. 3rd XI v Rodmersham CC (a) Nolan Wilde, ct Linder b Thompson, takes his 4th of the season and 25th career, drawing level with Dave Charlton (1988-2018). 4th XI v New Ash Green CC (h) Mohamed Safeer Ibra Lebbe (lbw b Mick Sumner) already has 3 ducks this season from just 3 career innings — an early and thorough education in the art of not scoring. Gene Smith (b Daryl Horton) reaches 4 for the season and 4 for his career, level with Matthew Ward (2011-2012). Sunday 16 August 1st XI v Grenfell CC (h) Jude Brooks, b Daiwik Singh off 4 balls, records his 2nd of the season and career, joining Alan Probert (2008-2009) — himself a rare double member of the Debutante and Retirement Duck boards. Jacob Landman survived 13 balls before falling ct Patel b Singireddy, his 2nd of the season and 3rd career. On this day in 1953, John Ames (1952-1978, 49 ducks) also departed for nought, against Mote A. Week in summary Nine ducks, eight matches, and Saturday doing the heavy lifting with seven of them spread across four different XIs — consistency of a very particular kind. Thomas Beeney remains the club's chief tormentor-in-chief this season. Duck Hunting Season leaderboard 🍩 1. Thomas Beeney — 9 ducks, 32 inns (28.1%) 2. Spencer Gray — 5 ducks, 22 inns (22.7%) 3. Brandon Eloff — 5 ducks, 24 inns (20.8%) 4. Anthony Karassellos — 5 ducks, 31 inns (16.1%) 5. Theo Clements — 5 ducks, 34 inns (14.7%) See you all next weekend — the honours board never sleeps, and there's always room for one more nought. 0️⃣🏏

🦆 DUCK REPORT — 5 to 12 August 2026

8 ducks
Week 17 · 5 Aug 2026 – 12 Aug 2026
Seven matches, eight ducks, and the exclusive zero club opened its gates once more to the unlucky, the unfortunate, and — twice this week — the entirely golden. A tidy week's harvest. 🏏 1st XI — Borstal CC (away, 8 Aug) A brace for the visitors. Darrell Houghton-Judge fell to Mohammed Azhar after five balls of stern resistance, his 1st duck of the season and 37th of a fine career (277 innings, 34th all-time) — level with Joshua Knowler, who played 2008–2025. Darrell remains a Full House nearly-man, one position shy of ducking right through the order. Last man Matthew Carter joined him moments later, bowled Sam Pepper, his own season-opener and 39th career duck from 316 innings (29th all-time) — level with Chris Newman (2002–2017). Carter is a paid-up Debutante Duck club member and a former Duck of the Year, class of 2004. 🏏 3rd XI — Bredgar CC (home, 8 Aug) Another double, this time at home. Trevor Back edged behind for his 2nd duck of the season and a mighty 95th career nought — 797 innings deep and 3rd on the all-time roll, a regular of the Ducks on the Road, Homebody and Lone Duck top tens. On this very day in 1998, Richard Piper (96 ducks, 2nd all-time) was doing much the same against Bearsted. Curtis Etherington kept him company, bowled Sophie Hogben for his maiden career duck in only his 3rd innings — level with the mysterious - Howard, whose entire Linton career back in 2006 amounted to exactly one. 🏏 Midweek XI — The Mote CC (away, 11 Aug) Theo Clements, bowled Ronak Patel, notched his 5th duck of the season and 15th career (109 innings) — level with Richard Knowler, 2004–2026. 🌞 Sunday 1st XI — Stone-in-Oxney CC (home, 9 Aug) Praveen Tunga went first ball to Toby Withers Green — a golden duck, the purest form of the art — his 4th of the season and 10th career, from the Only Two Quacks board alongside Brandon Eloff. On this day in 1964, John Thirkell (90 ducks, 5th all-time) fell for nought against Harrietsham. 🌞 Sunday 2nd XI — Westerham CC (away, 9 Aug) Two more out at Westerham. Reuben Mundell was caught off Arhum Khan for his 1st duck of the season and 5th career — level with Alex Holt (2022–2026) — and comes from proper duck-collecting stock, sibling Thomas Mundell sat on 8 career noughts and a parent-child pairing with Blair Mundell on 3. Then Alexander Nunn, first ball, bowled Ishtiaq Azram — a second golden duck for the week — his 3rd of the season and 10th career, another to share Thirkell's 1964 date with Harrietsham. 📋 Week in Summary 8 ducks from 7 matches, and a curious symmetry: three fixtures — Borstal, Bredgar and Westerham — each produced a matching pair, and two victims never got off the mark at all. Consistency of a very particular kind. 🏆 Duck Hunting Season leaderboard 1. Thomas Beeney — 8 ducks/30 inn (26.67%) 2. Spencer Gray — 5/21 (23.81%) 3. Brandon Eloff — 5/23 (21.74%) 4. Anthony Karassellos — 5/29 (17.24%) 5. Theo Clements — 5/31 (16.13%) Next fixture looms, and with it, no doubt, fresh additions to the honours board. See you at the crease — or not, as the case may be. 🦆🍩

🦆 LPCC Duck Club — Week of 28 July to 4 August 2026

4 ducks
Week 16 · 28 Jul 2026 – 4 Aug 2026
Only four members qualified for admission this week, but nine matches gave everyone every chance, and the Club never turns away a genuine effort. Quality over quantity, as the exclusive zero club likes to say. Sunday 2nd XI — home to Boughton & Eastwell CC Jacob Landman, in at six, fell b Christopher Francis for his 1st duck of the season and 2nd of an increasingly distinguished career, from just 7 innings. Jacob remains a paid-up member of the Debutante Duck club courtesy of a first-baller some time back, and now draws level with Alan Probert, who played 2008 to 2009 and reached the very same tally of 2 in only 2 innings, before promptly retiring on a duck himself. Some finish what they start. At number 11, Alexander Nunn joined him, bowled by Archie Rushin for his 2nd of the season and 9th career duck from 32 innings. That's level with Charles Curteis, a name from 2016 to 2020 who took 50 innings to get there — Alexander is getting to the same dubious distinction at rather more pace. The Hundred — away to Egerton CC, Kent Tim Ludick strode out at first drop and was back in the shed before he'd got comfortable — first ball, bowled Cameron Clarke, a proper golden duck. It's his maiden career nought from 9 innings and his 1st of the season, and it sits him alongside - Howard, whose single career duck came in 2006 in his only innings for the club, before he too bowed out for good. Tim will be hoping his own Duck Club membership runs rather longer. Brandon Eloff, at six, survived a couple of deliveries before edging Tom Richards — his 5th duck of the season and 13th of his career, 109th on the all-time list. That draws him level with Joe Martin, who played 2004 to 2016 and needed 86 innings to reach 13 where Brandon's done it in 77 — triumph through adversity, and rapid triumph at that. Brandon isn't fighting this alone either: fellow duck-club members Johan Eloff (14 career ducks) and Christian Eloff (3) share the family name, though neither troubled the scorers this week. He also remains a standing member of the Only Two Quacks club alongside Praveen Tunga. Week in Summary Four ducks from nine matches — the art of not scoring practised sparingly this week. Boughton & Eastwell and Egerton both took their toll, and Brandon Eloff continues to make a serious fist of the season race. Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard 🥇🍩 - Thomas Beeney — 8 ducks, 27 innings, 29.63% - Spencer Gray — 5 ducks, 20 innings, 25.00% - Brandon Eloff — 5 ducks, 23 innings, 21.74% - Anthony Karassellos — 5 ducks, 27 innings, 18.52% - David Holdstock — 4 ducks, 5 innings, 80.00% Spare a thought for David Holdstock, quietly running the most alarming strike rate in the club without yet cracking the summit. Next fixture, same open invitation: middle stump, minimal footwork, maximum glory. The honours board awaits its next volunteer. 0️⃣🏏

🦆 Duck News — Week of 21–27 July

6 ducks
Week 15 · 21 Jul 2026 – 27 Jul 2026
Six ducks fell across eight fixtures this week, with Marden serving up a golden double. Here's who joined the exclusive zero club. 🏏 Saturday — 1st XI v Whitstable CC (home) Alex Keeler got things underway, bowled by Andrew Bennett for 3 balls faced — his first duck of the season and the 16th of a fine career, level with Alex Wade (2014–2026, 16 from 133) at 93rd/94th all-time. Bennett wasn't done. Nick Pennefather edged behind to Paul Gambrill after seven balls for his 3rd duck of the campaign and 10th for the club from 55 innings — level with Jack Jenner (2003–2008, 10 from 53). Nick remains a card-carrying Debutante Duck from his own first-baller days, with sibling Neill Pennefather (2 career ducks) keeping it in the family. 🥇 Saturday — 2nd XI v Marden CC, Kent (away) A golden double at Marden. Brandon Eloff was lbw to Edward Chapman first ball — his 4th of the season, 12th of his career from 75 innings, level with Gareth Davies (2003–2013, 12 from 77). Last man Praveen Tunga matched him stroke for non-stroke, stumped off his very first delivery for his own 3rd duck of the season and 9th of his career from just 34 innings, joining Charles Curteis (2016–2020, 9 from 50). The pair already share the club's Only Two Quacks honour — and having golden-ducked in the very same innings, they've given the ledger fresh material. Brandon's boys keep it a family trade too: Johan Eloff (14 career ducks) and Christian Eloff (3), both fellow members in good standing. 📅 Sunday — 1st XI v Newenden CC (away) Thomas Beeney, bowled by Finnian Piper, chalks up his 8th duck of the season and 57th of an imperious career — 10th on the all-time roll from 350 innings, a timely reminder his Duck of the Year 2026 crown sits firmly in place. On this very day in 2008, Tom Murphy was up to the same tricks against Rumwood CC, en route to 11 career ducks. Father Michael Beeney (38 career noughts) watches on with quiet pride. 🍩 Sunday — 2nd XI v Milstead CC (home) David Holdstock, caught behind off Edward Rowe after 4 balls, notches his 4th duck of the season — his 4th in just 4 innings for the club, a flawless record already good for 247th all-time. He joins Matthew Ward (2011–2012, 4 from 10) on the same tally. LPCC Duck Hunting Season 2026 – Week 4 Report

14 ducks
Week 4 · 9 May 2026 – 10 May 2026
Six matches this week — four league fixtures on Saturday and two games on Sunday — provided ample opportunity for ducks to flourish. But did the weekend live up to expectations? We dive into the scorecards to see who now leads the charge for Duck of the Year 2026 and whether any of Duck Club’s more obscure subcategories gained new members. --- Double Duck Weekend Propels a New Leader We begin with the crushing 1st XI defeat away to Lordswood Cricket Club. Runs were plentiful, unfortunately only for Lordswood. Three Linton batsmen managed to scramble a single run to avoid adding to their duck tallies. I was not among them. Saturday’s dismissal without scoring brought my career total to 51 ducks, drawing level with John Karassellos and Ian Brattle. However, I did not remain there for long. What better way to honour Ian Brattle — the holder of the legendary six consecutive ducks in the 1975 season — than with a double duck weekend? Another duck on Sunday saw me bunny-hop over both JK and Brattle to reach 52 career ducks. This milestone also places me alongside Luke Welsman who holds the exclusive and highly prestigious “50 Ducks Before Age 30” category. More importantly, I now emerge as the outright leader in the 2026 Duck of the Year standings with three ducks for the season. JK will have his work cut out if he is to retain the Duck of the Year trophy he won in 2025. --- Second XI – A Rare Duckless Affair The 2nd XI produced a disappointingly duck-free scorecard, so we move swiftly on. --- Third XI – Four Ducks and Two New Members The 3rd XI more than compensated for the Second Team’s restraint, recording four ducks: * Euan Beardwell * Spencer Gray * Paul Baker * Tim Thirkell Tim Thirkell – King of the Ducks Tim continues to soar above the flock with an astonishing 104 career ducks. It is lonely at the summit. Euan Beardwell Euan records his fourth senior duck for Linton across four seasons, drawing level with Matt Ward, who remarkably accumulated all four of his ducks in his final season before quietly departing the game. Spencer Gray Spencer was joined by both sons, Will Gray and James Gray. Sadly, only the father succumbed, meaning the coveted Father and Son Duck and Family of Ducks categories remain unchanged. Paul Baker A second father-and-son combination featured, with Dan Baker playing alongside his father Paul. Again, only the elder Baker was tempted by the duck. Both Spencer Gray and Paul Baker record their first ducks for the club and are formally inducktrinated into the LPCC Duck Family. --- Fourth XI – Dr Safeer Strikes Again Dr Safeer recorded his second duck of the season against the Orpington Ocelots, lasting seven balls before departing. This brings him level with Louis Turney on two career ducks. --- Sunday Cricket – A Hen Appears On Sunday, Claire Rootes departed without troubling the scorers. As Duck Club is an inclusive institution, Claire becomes the latest member and earns recognition as a Hen — the female equivalent of a duck. --- NVKO Update The NVKO fixture against Addington Cricket Club was conceded, granting Linton a bye into the next round where we will face Chestfield Cricket Club. Following last week’s encounter in the KVCL, we are hoping for a more favourable outcome. --- Sunday 1st XI – Another for the Author, and Ian Hollingworth Joins the Party The Sunday 1st XI fixture, moved to Rumwood, delivered two late-order ducks: * Myself (completing the double duck weekend) * Ian Hollingworth For a player with over two decades at the Park and a famously gung-ho approach to batting, it is remarkable Ian has not featured more prominently in Duck Club lore. This was Ian’s 35th career duck, drawing him level with Stan Wratton, whose extraordinary Linton career spanned more than 40 years. --- Sunday 2nd XI Collapse – Four More Ducks The Sunday 2nd XI were bowled out for 66, producing another rich harvest. Noah Stevens Noah Stevens recorded his second adult duck for the club. Nolan and Zach Wilde Nolan Wilde and Zach Wilde both fell for ducks while playing together. This earns them a place in Duck Club Hall of Fame under the prestigious Father and Son Duck category. Jamie Wheeler Jamie Wheeler recorded his first adult duck and is warmly welcomed into the LPCC Duck Club. --- Duck of the Year 2026 Standings (After Week 4) 1. Tom Beeney – 3 ducks 2. John Karassellos – 2 ducks 3. Dr Safeer – 2 ducks 4. Noah Stevens – 2 ducks 5. Nolan Wilde – 1 duck 6. Zach Wilde – 1 duck 7. Jamie Wheeler – 1 duck 8. Will Gray – 1 duck 9. Spencer Gray – 1 duck 10. Paul Baker – 1 duck 11. Claire Rootes – 1 hen --- The season is still young, but the field is beginning to take shape. With a commanding lead and momentum firmly on my side, the question on everyone’s lips is simple: Can anyone stop me from claiming Duck of the Year 2026?

LPCC Duck Hunt 2026 – Week 3 Update

3 ducks
Week 3 · 2 May 2026 – 3 May 2026
A new leader has emerged in the race for LPCC Duck of the Year 2026. With last week’s duck still fresh in the memory, John Karassellos rose to the occasion on Sunday in the 2nd XI fixture against Marden… by adding another. Marden piled on 307, which proved far too much, with the 2s bowled out for 124 in reply. Included in that total was JK’s second duck of the season — and his 51st all-time. That milestone sees him pull clear of the pack and draw level with Ian Brattle, who holds a special place in Duck Club folklore for one of the most remarkable records: six consecutive ducks during the 1975 season at the Park. Brattle also features in the exclusive “50 ducks before a 50” subcategory — a club so niche it still only has two members. JK, of course, was Duck of the Year 2025. While he’s made an early statement, the season is young — plenty of time for a recovery… or for others to reel him in. In a match that promised much for Duck Club subcategories, Russel Wilde returned to the LPCC side, representing the wider Wilde family alongside Nolan and Zach. Russel, already etched into history with a Debutante Duck back in 2022, didn’t disappoint — now sitting on 2 ducks from just 3 appearances. However, with no ducks for Nolan or Zach, the coveted “Family of Ducks” category remains unchanged… for now. Russel is certainly one to watch. Elsewhere, on Saturday, Will Gray recorded his first duck of the season in his third game, earning a place on this year’s leaderboard. Will now has 6 adult ducks for Linton (a reminder: junior ducks don’t count towards official totals), drawing level with Mick Filmer. Filmer’s career is notable not just for its longevity, but for its curious duck-free comebacks — returning after breaks in 1988 and again in 1993 without adding to his tally. A man who knew when to avoid the spotlight. No other ducks were recorded on a rain-affected Saturday.

🦆 Duck Club Returns – Opening Weekend 2026

5 ducks
Week 1 · 18 Apr 2026 – 19 Apr 2026
Welcome back to another glorious Duck Hunting season at Linton Park Cricket Club! The 2026 campaign got underway in style this weekend and, crucially, did not disappoint. With five matches across Saturday and Sunday, there was no shortage of opportunity for those dreaded—but celebrated—ducks. As always, best to get those naughty noughts out of the system before the league season fires up in May. And I’m pleased to report… the Duck Club is already thriving. 🏏 Saturday – Bearsted Battles & Early Casualties Linton Park kicked things off with a full club double-header against local rivals Bearsted, with fixtures home and away. At Bearsted Green, the 1st XI got underway. Duck Club regular Jordan Austin opened proceedings and narrowly avoided early honours, grafting his way to 2 before being trapped in front by Alex Lush. Unfortunately, Johan Eloff wasn’t as fortunate—registering the first duck of the 2026 season. A strong start to the campaign for Johan, who now moves to 12 career ducks in just 52 innings, boasting an impressive 23% duck rate. He draws level with LPCC great Burt Buckoke, whose four-decade career (1928–1954) yielded the same tally in 55 innings. All eyes will be on Johan this season to see how far he can push that number. Not to be outdone, Sam Boyns also added to his collection, bringing up his 12th duck for the club. With 148 innings under his belt, Sam maintains a respectable 8% duck rate, now level with Martin Larkin, a familiar name from the 80s and 90s, who reached the same milestone in just 70 innings (albeit better known for his exploits with the ball). 🔥 2nd XI – A Hall of Fame Moment Meanwhile, back at home against Bearsted 2nd XI, things truly heated up. In the closing stages of the innings, chasing quick bonus runs and glory, I strode to the crease with intent… and departed just as quickly. A thick edge, a simple catch, and history was made. Duck number 50. A milestone moment. Bat raised. Crowd (mostly) silent. This achievement secures formal entry into the Duck Club Hall of Fame—an elite gathering of individuals whose ability to accumulate the dreaded duck is unmatched. This landmark innings moves me to 15th in the all-time standings, surpassing David Castle and drawing level with fellow Duck Club member Jordan Austin. Together, we now stand alongside John Ames (1952–1978), who recorded 50 ducks across 418 innings. For context: My 50 ducks: 327 innings (15%) Ames’ 50 ducks: 418 innings Efficiency matters. 🏏 3rd XI – Into Double Figures The 3rd XI clash with Brasted Chart & Toys Hill added another name to the honours board. Jonno Sisely brought up his 10th LPCC duck in just 27 innings, joining the ranks of Theo Clements (present), Brian Fuller (1968–1976), and Don Hartridge (1940–1952). A fine achievement—and a reminder that no one is ever truly alone in the Duck Club. And for perspective, things could always be worse. Special mention must go to Magnus Boxer and E Hayes, who maintain a flawless 100% duck rate. Truly remarkable consistency. 🌱 Sunday – A Mixed Bag Sunday’s fixtures provided a quieter, more selective harvest. The 1st XI emergency fixture against Mallu was, disappointingly, a vegan affair—completely free from fowl. However, the 2nd XI trip to Rumwood to face New Ifield delivered one addition: Alex Nunn – now on 10 career ducks (45 innings), joining Jonno in double figures. Near misses came from Zach Wilde and Nolan Wilde, both falling for 1. A single run away from Duck Club folklore—particularly in what would have been a rare and celebrated Father & Son Duck double. Plenty of time for that yet… 📅 Looking Ahead A strong opening weekend for the Duck Club, with milestones, new members, and early-season form all on display. With the league season fast approaching, the question remains: Who will rise (or fall) to the occasion next weekend? We watch. We wait. We celebrate. 🦆

1963 Season 13 reports

🦆 Duck News — 20 to 23 July 1963 🦆

6 ducks
Week 13 · 20 Jul 1963 – 23 Jul 1963
🏏 Saturday, 1st XI v Rumwood CC (h) A vintage afternoon for the exclusive zero club, as four Linton batsmen queued up to demonstrate the art of not scoring. Basil Sears led the way, caught Mike Iliffe bowled B- Hayes — his 2nd duck of the season and 17th of an increasingly decorated career, good enough for 12th of 777 in the all-time roll. Splendidly, on this very day back in 1906, R W Mitchell was doing precisely the same thing against the Royal West Kent Regiment CC Officers' XI. Some habits span the centuries. David Gale, bowled John Carter, banked his 3rd of the season and 3rd of his career alike — level pegging, as career and season are still one and the same for our newest addition. He too keeps Mitchell's 1906 company today, though as we'll see, Rumwood-week wasn't done with him yet. Barry Langridge fell bowled B- Buckland for his 2nd of the season and career, joining Mitchell's 1906 club for a third time this innings. A paid-up member of this year's Quacked by Kin honours besides, having watched father Dick Langridge notch his own duck earlier in 1963 — the family evidently believes in shared hobbies. And then, majestically, Bob Arnold — bowled John Carter for his 5th duck of the season, taking a career tally of 44 that stands 2nd of 777 all-time. Arnold sits proudly atop the Duck of the Year 1963 table, with a Ducks in a Row honour and a Quacking Together nod alongside John Thirkell already banked. A genuine great of the format, and Mitchell's fourth companion of the day. 🏏 Wednesday, Midweek XI v Senacre Staff XI (h) Gordon Fenner was undone by Cridland for his 1st duck of the season, his 19th in 157 innings and 8th of 777 all-time — a family trade, with siblings Joe (5 career ducks) and Maurice (1) also enrolled. He shares his date with Brian Relf, who ducked against Tovil on this same day back in 1960. And returning for an unwelcome encore, David Gale fell bowled Tucker for his 4th of the season and career — a proper pair for the week, Rumwood to Senacre without so much as troubling the scoreboard in between. Two matches, two ducks, nought to show for either. 📋 Week in Summary Six ducks in three matches, with Rumwood doing the early damage and Senacre mopping up midweek. No golden ducks and no king pairs to report, but David Gale's grim double and Bob Arnold's continued assault on the club's all-time summit gave the week its shape. Consistency of a very particular kind. 🥇 Duck Hunting Season leaderboard - Bob Arnold — 6 innings, 5 ducks, 83.33% - David Gale — 13 innings, 4 ducks, 30.77% - John Thirkell — 19 innings, 4 ducks, 21.05% - Michael Chambers — 8 innings, 3 ducks, 37.5% - William Buck — 9 innings, 3 ducks, 33.33% Arnold's grip on the top spot looks vice-like for now, but the season's still young. Get yourselves out to the middle this weekend, gentlemen — the club's zero column is always open for new subscribers. 🍩0️⃣

🦆 Duck Report — 13th & 14th July 1963

2 ducks
Week 12 · 13 Jul 1963 – 14 Jul 1963
A slim but characterful haul this week — just the two ducks, though both come from players with plenty of previous. Saturday 13th July — 1st XI v Terry Whittaker's XI Terry Whittaker, batting at 11, fell to the wonderfully self-referential dismissal "b Terry Whittaker" — presumably a namesake with the ball, though the Duck Club never asks too many questions. It's his 1st duck of the season and 12th of a career now spanning 81 innings, good enough for 23rd on the all-time list of 776. Terry remains a paid-up member of Quacking Together (with Brian Relf) and, more solemnly, of the Retirement Duck club — a standing honour from a past farewell, no comment on his future. On this very day in 1940, Ernie Chiesman also departed for nought, against Loose CC, en route to 2 career ducks across a stint running 1940 to 1956. Sunday 14th July — 1st XI v Anchorians CC Opener John Ames didn't trouble the scorers either, caught P- Lawrence bowled B- Snelling for his 1st duck of the season and 28th of his career — 206 innings deep and sitting a mighty 4th of 776 all time. John's honours board reads like a small trophy cabinet: Ducks in a Row (four consecutive, no less), a place in the Homebody Duck top 10, and shared quacking credits with Alan Wilkes, Roy Clarke and Stan Wratten. Fittingly, on this day in 1956, A Hughes also fell for nought against A.Trembeths, on his way to a solitary career duck and a spot in the Debutante Duck club. Week in Summary Two matches, two ducks, both courtesy of the 1st XI on successive days — a tidy weekend's work for the Club, if not for the batsmen. No pairs, no family affairs, nothing golden — just honest, top-order and tail-end failure in equal measure. Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard - Bob Arnold — 4 ducks in 5 innings (80%) - John Thirkell — 4 ducks in 18 innings (22.22%) - Michael Chambers — 3 ducks in 7 innings (42.86%) - William Buck — 3 ducks in 9 innings (33.33%) - Roy Clarke — 3 ducks in 18 innings (16.67%) Bob Arnold sets the pace with a frankly alarming 80% strike rate for failure — the rest of the chasing pack will need to pull their socks up, or their pads off, if they're to catch him. Next match, next chance. The Duck Club never sleeps — see you at the crease. 🦆🍩 --- Unrelated to the above: one of the team's machines (turbosammy-Defiance-Pro-16) is well behind on shared config and flagging unresolved problems — worth a nudge to whoever owns it to open a session, which will pull automatically.

🦆 DUCK REPORT — Sunday, 7th July 1963

4 ducks
Week 11 · 7 Jul 1963
A grim afternoon away at Aylesford Paper Mills CC, where one bowler did the lot. Colin Watson helped himself to four Linton wickets, every one of them bowled, every one of them for nought. The exclusive zero club welcomes four fresh entries in a single innings — a proper cluster of quacking. 1st XI — away to Aylesford Paper Mills CC Stan Wratten (3) fell b Colin Watson, his 2nd duck of the season and 19th of a long career spanning 219 innings — 8th in the all-time standings, where he still shares "Quacking Together" honours with club great John Ames. On this very day in 1906, B W Haynes (1891–1910) was also dismissed for nought, against Sutton Valence School — history repeating itself to the day. Len Conway (4) followed, b Colin Watson, his 2nd of the season and 10th career duck from 98 innings, 28th all-time. A long-standing member of the Debutante Duck club from his own first-ever innings, Len shares that same eerie calendar echo — 7th July 1906, B W Haynes, Sutton Valence School — proving some dates simply belong to the ducks. John Thirkell (6) then departed, b Colin Watson, his 4th duck of the season and, more significantly, his 50th career duck — Full Membership of the Hall of Fame secured, and from 433 innings he now sits 1st in the entire all-time standings of 776 entries, a colossus of the art of not scoring. Three Duck of the Year titles (1952, 1954, 1955) and top-10 placings in Lone Duck, Homebody Duck and Ducks on the Road round out a truly imperial collection. Fittingly, his old "Quacking Together" partner William Buck fell in this very innings too — old comrades reunited in ignominy. William Buck (7) completed the rout, b Colin Watson, his 3rd of the season and 21st career duck from 257 innings, 7th all-time — drawing level with Robert Wood (1958–1963, 151 innings) on the same tally. As the honours board already knew, William's name sits paired with John Thirkell's — and today they proved it wasn't just paperwork. Week in Summary One match, one rampant bowler, four ducks — the entire tally supplied by a single Aylesford spell. Positions 3, 4, 6 and 7 all back in the pavilion without troubling the scorer. Colin Watson will not be remembered fondly at Linton Park. 🏆 Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard 1. Bob Arnold — 4 ducks / 5 innings (80.0%) 2. John Thirkell — 4 ducks / 18 innings (22.22%) 3. Michael Chambers — 3 ducks / 7 innings (42.86%) 4. William Buck — 3 ducks / 9 innings (33.33%) 5. Roy Clarke — 3 ducks / 17 innings (17.65%) 🍩 The season presses on, and with it the race for Duck of the Year. Roll on the next fixture — the ducks are surely just getting started. 0️⃣🏏

🦆 Duck Report — 30 June 1963

5 ducks
Week 10 · 30 Jun 1963
Just the one fixture on the books this week, but Tilling Steven at home proved fertile hunting ground for the exclusive zero club — five ducks in a single innings, two of them from the very same household. Not a bad afternoon's work for a place of dubious distinction. 🏏 1st XI v Tilling Steven (Home) Oddly, every departure today shares the same footnote in the record books: on this very day back in 1956, R- Robinson also trudged back for nought against St Lukes Maidstone CC. Some anniversaries you plan for. This plainly wasn't one of them. The top order wobbled early. William Buck fell to R- Bailey for their 2nd duck of the season, moving to a lofty 20 career ducks — 7th on the all-time list of 776. Buck shares the "Quacking Together" board with today's next victim, John Thirkell, and the pair are evidently determined to keep the tradition alive in person as well as on paper. Speaking of which — Thirkell followed almost immediately, bowled by Fred Baker for their 3rd duck of the campaign. Thirkell sits utterly alone at the summit of the all-time charts, an imperious 49 ducks from 432 innings, a three-time Duck of the Year (1952, 1954, 1955) and a fixture of the Lone Duck, Homebody Duck and Ducks on the Road top tens. Fifty — and Full Membership — looms. They also sit 4th in this season's own Duck Hunting race. X Rayner chipped in with a 1st duck of the season, lbw to Bailey, and now carries 2 from a brutal 3 career innings — a paid-up, if premature-sounding, member of the Retirement Duck club from a past farewell, though there's plainly plenty of cricket left in them yet. Then came the afternoon's real ceremony. Dick Langridge (bowled Baker, their 2nd duck of the season and 2nd of their career) was followed to the middle — and straight back to the pavilion — by fellow Langridge Barry (lbw Bailey, their 1st senior duck). Together they completed a Duck and Ducklings double: a parent and child brought down in the very same innings, the rarest ceremony the club offers, now permanently enshrined on Barry's honours board as "Quacked by Kin". One over, two Langridges, nought between them. 📊 Week in Summary One match, five ducks, and a family entry to boot — Bailey and Baker shared the damage for Tilling Steven between them. The Langridge household will want a quiet word before next weekend. 🏆 Duck Hunting Season leaderboard 1. Bob Arnold — 4 ducks / 5 innings (80%) 2. Michael Chambers — 3 ducks / 6 innings (50%) 3. Roy Clarke — 3 ducks / 16 innings (18.75%) 4. John Thirkell — 3 ducks / 17 innings (17.65%) 5. C- Haylor — 2 ducks / 2 innings (100%) Bring on the next fixture — the ducks are circling, and the club stands ready to welcome its newest, and most persistent, members. 🍩0️⃣🦆

🦆 Duck News — Weekend of 22–23 June, 1963

3 ducks
Week 9 · 22 Jun 1963 – 23 Jun 1963
A quieter weekend for the Duck Club overall, but the 1st XI did their bit to keep the honours board ticking over with a tidy hat-trick of noughts across two fixtures. 🏏 Saturday 22 June — Rumwood CC (away) 1st XI's day at Rumwood brought first blood for the weekend. In at five, C- Haylor was undone by John Carter and trudged back for nought — his 12th career duck, good enough for 19th on the all-time list of 776. Haylor already carries the 1963 Runaway Duck watch on his CV, a whole campaign without troubling the scorers, and this one keeps that grim ledger open for business. Curiously, on this very day back in 1935, Percy Brattle — who turned out for the club from 1934 to 1962 — also strolled back for a duck, one of five in a career now sitting 56th all-time. Some things, it seems, are written in the calendar. 🏏 Sunday 23 June — Maidstone AKCC (home) Home comforts proved no comfort at all, with two more names added to the weekend's tally. C- Haylor was back at it, bowled by Terry Whittaker at number six for his 13th career duck — and, notably, his second in as many days. That completes a proper pair for the weekend, not quite the rarefied air of a king pair, but a grim brace of blobs all the same. On this same day in 1906, club stalwart Jack Fryer — twice Duck of the Year, in 1891 and 1900 no less — also made a duck of his own on the way to a career total of 12. Down at 11, Ossie Fryer fell to Eddie Page, chalking up his first duck of the season and only his second in a career still finding its feet at 7 innings — 147th on the all-time roll of dishonour. Fittingly, he shares this day in history with a fellow Fryer, Jack, though the record shows no family link between the two — just a shared surname and a shared fondness, apparently, for late-June ducks. 📋 Week in Summary Three ducks from two matches, the lot of them courtesy of the 1st XI, with C- Haylor doing the damage twice over for a weekend pair. Quiet elsewhere, but the season's engine keeps turning. 🥇 Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard - Bob Arnold — 4 ducks from 5 innings (80%) - Michael Chambers — 3 ducks from 5 innings (60%) - Roy Clarke — 3 ducks from 15 innings (20%) - C- Haylor — 2 ducks from 2 innings (100%) - E- Bevan — 2 ducks from 2 innings (100%) Bob Arnold sits pretty at the summit, but with Haylor now perfect at 100% for the season, the chasing pack will want to watch their backs. Week 8 · 15 Jun 1963 – 16 Jun 1963
A modest weekend in the annals of the exclusive zero club, but three names were added to the ledger all the same — and one of them was doing it in a losing cause against Bobbing Court, always the way. 🏏 1st XI Saturday at Headcorn saw Roy Clarke depart for nought, caught L Woodcock off S Parnham at first drop, his third of the season and his 28th career duck — a tally that keeps him a very solid 4th of 776 on the all-time list, a rarefied altitude few ever reach. Roy remains a paid-up member of the 1959 Duck of the Year honours board and stands shoulder to shoulder with John Ames in the Quacking Together club. And on this very day back in 1887, Jack Fryer — twice Duck of the Year himself in the 1890s — was making his own duck against 1st Innings East Peckham CC. History does love to repeat itself on a calendar. Sunday's away trip to Bobbing Court proved unkind to the middle and lower order. William Buck fell for his first of the season, caught C Robinson bowled P Bedelle, taking him to 19 career ducks — 8th of 776 all-time, and level company with Tony Snell, the 1958 Duck of the Year himself, who reached the same 19 in just 58 innings between 1952 and 1960. William also carries the Quacking Together honour alongside John Thirkell. Neatly enough, on this same date in 1951, the legendary Bob Arnold — Duck of the Year 1963 no less, and still active this very season — was also walking back against Maths School Rochester on his way to what is now 43 career ducks. Michael Chambers completed the misery at Bobbing Court, caught P Goodwin bowled P Bedelle at number ten, his third duck of the season and sixth of his career — a tidy little cluster that puts him level with a small crowd on exactly six, including the unfortunate Frank Wright, who managed the rare and dubious Quack-to-Quack double of duck on debut and duck on farewell. Michael, mercifully, remains very much an active concern. His parallel is the same Bob Arnold fixture of 1951 — quite the popular calendar date for ducks, it would seem. 📊 Week in Summary Two matches, three ducks, and Bobbing Court doing the lion's share of the damage with a brace in one innings. No pairs, no family affairs this week — just honest, workmanlike failure with the bat, the kind this club was built to celebrate. 🥇 Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard — 1963 1. Bob Arnold — 4 ducks in 5 innings (80%) 2. Michael Chambers — 3 in 5 (60%) 3. Roy Clarke — 3 in 13 (23.08%) 4. E- Bevan — 2 in 2 (100%) 5. David Gale — 2 in 6 (33.33%) Bob Arnold sets the pace by some distance, though E- Bevan's flawless 100% record from just two innings is the sort of consistency the club can only applaud. Plenty of season left for the standings to shuffle — bring on the next fixture and let's see who else the ducks come calling for. 🦆🏏0️⃣

🦆 Duck Report — Saturday 8th & Sunday 9th June 1963 🦆

3 ducks
Week 7 · 8 Jun 1963 – 9 Jun 1963
The 1963 season rolls on and the exclusive zero club welcomed three new entries across the weekend's two fixtures. Tovil and Gore Court CC both took their pound of Linton flesh — or rather, their nought. 🏏 Saturday 8th — 1st XI v Tovil (Home) E- Bevan, in at 7, was bowled by M- Taylor without so much as a nudge to get going. His second duck of the campaign, and remarkably his second in as many career innings — a Debutante Duck whose maiden knock was also a blob, meaning the LPCC scorebook has yet to see him trouble it at all. That's 2 from 2, rank 125 of 776 in the all-time reckoning. Fittingly, on this very day in 1940, Stan Pierce (1939–1946) was also walking back for nought, against Loose CC. Not to be outdone, Bob Arnold departed for the fourth time this season, caught Banes off White. Duck number 43 for his career moves him to a staggering 2nd of 776 all-time, propped up by his "Ducks in a Row" honour of four on the bounce and his standing as reigning Duck of the Year 1963 — a title looking increasingly secure. He too shares Stan Pierce's 1940 date with Loose CC as his on-this-day companion, and remains a card-carrying member of the club's Quacking Together fraternity alongside John Thirkell. 🌱 Sunday 9th — 1st XI v Gore Court CC (Away) Ron Hickman, at 9, was caught Cutmore off the bowling of Gerald Lukehurst for his first duck of the season and just his second in senior colours from two innings — rank 313 of 776. A quieter entry to the club, but a member nonetheless, alongside his Quacking Together billing with Alan Cradduck. Bob Arnold continues to make the Duck of the Year race very much his own — four ducks and counting, and nobody else is close. 3 ducks
Week 6 · 1 Jun 1963 – 7 Jun 1963
A quieter week in the paddock, but the Duck Club's ledger never rests. Three fresh entries this week, and a bowler at Folkestone who fancied himself a specialist. 1st XI Saturday, home to A.Trembeths — Bob Arnold strode out at seven and departed as he so often does, bowled by B- Stalley without deposit. It's his 3rd duck of the season already, and his 42nd career quack from 184 innings, keeping him lodged at a magnificent 2nd on the all-time list. With three ducks from three attempts this season he's currently 100% on brand and sits top of the Duck of the Year table — the honours board already has his name pencilled in for 1963, and he's riding a streak entered on the board as Ducks in a Row (4 consecutive), which is either a tremendous achievement or a cry for help. On this very day in 1903, Rev W A Carr was doing much the same thing against Maidstone CC — some traditions span the centuries. Sunday, home to Folkestone CC — Gerald Jeanes evidently decided two wickets for nought was a fair afternoon's work. First to fall was Len Conway at first drop, trapped lbw without scoring for his 1st duck of the season and 9th of an increasingly distinguished career from 96 innings, good enough for 32nd all-time. Len is, of course, a long-serving member of the Debutante Duck club, having opened his account with a nought on his own first-ever appearance — old habits. On this day in 1962, Basil Sears was likewise walking back for nought against A.Trembeths. In walked Terry Donovan at three, and out he went too, bowled by the same relentless Jeanes for his very first career duck in 9 innings — number 328 on the all-time list and a debut entry to the club proper, though not his cricketing debut, mind. Terry remains agonisingly close to the Full House nearly-man board, having now batted in 10 of the 11 possible positions — number eleven awaits. Fittingly, Basil Sears also made his mark on this exact date back in 1962. Week in Summary Three ducks from four matches, two of them back-to-back at Folkestone courtesy of one persistent Mr Jeanes — a fine early rehearsal for anyone hoping to open the bowling averages this season. Bob Arnold continues to make the Duck of the Year race look like a foregone conclusion. Then Bob Arnold, bowled John Ames at nine, his 2nd of the season and 41st for the club, 2nd on the all-time chart. With two from two this term Bob currently leads the 1963 Duck of the Year race, sits proudly on Ducks in a Row for four consecutive, and holds Quacking Together status with both Alan Wilkes and John Thirkell. Stan Wratten kept him company, bowled W Webb at six, his 1st duck of the season and 18th of his career — 10th on the all-time list, and another Quacking Together entry alongside John Ames. 6 ducks
Week 2 · 5 May 1963 – 8 May 1963
A brutal double-header against West Farleigh CC, home and away, and the ducks came thick and fast — six of them in two matches, with one bowler doing most of the damage. 1st XI Saturday at home, West Farleigh's Peter J Day had himself a field day, bowling three Linton batsmen for nought and trapping a fourth lbw inside the same innings — a proper procession through the top order. - Frank Brattle (b Peter J Day) opened and fell for his 1st duck of the season, 18th of a career that now sits 8th on the all-time list of 772 — a chip off the old block, with kinsman Percy Brattle carrying 5 career ducks of his own. On this day in 1956, Richard Harris was doing exactly the same thing against Marden CC, en route to a barnstorming 36. - Robert Murray (b Peter J Day) followed him back for his 1st of the season, 14th career, 18th all-time. Same date, seven years earlier, Richard Harris was also making a duck — against Marden CC rather than West Farleigh. - Richard Ashby (lbw b Peter J Day) fell for his 1st this season and 3rd career, 102nd all-time, and remains a paid-up member of both the Ducks in a Row club (five on the spin) and the Tourist Duck top 10 — a man who travels well, just not with the bat. Harris's 1956 effort keeps him company on the anniversary front. - David Gale (b Micky Back) broke Day's stranglehold only in name — Micky Back finished the job — for his 1st ever senior duck in 14 innings, 209th all-time. The date belongs to Harris again, 1956, against Marden. - Michael Chambers (b Peter J Day) rounded off the innings with his 2nd duck of the season already, moving to 5 career and 55th all-time. A fifth appearance for Harris's 1956 duck on this same May date. Over at the return fixture on the Wednesday, away this time, Dick Langridge (b Ray Ford) picked up his 1st senior duck from just 6 innings, 210th all-time. On this day in 1960, Alan Wilkes was doing likewise against Halfway House — one of only two clubs ever to get him, Bob Arnold and John Ames sharing that dubious "Only Two Quacks" double. Week in Summary Six ducks from two matches against the same opponents, four of them off the same over-worked arm of Peter J Day, who might fairly claim honorary Duck Club membership for services rendered. West Farleigh clearly enjoyed themselves. 🦆 Duck Report — 27–28 April 1963

5 ducks
Week 1 · 27 Apr 1963 – 28 Apr 1963
Two fixtures, five noughts, and Linton's 1st XI doing all the damage to themselves this week. The zero club welcomes fresh blood and old faithfuls alike. 🏏 Saturday 27th — away to West Farleigh CC A rough afternoon at the crease, with West Farleigh's Ron Kemp helping himself to three LPCC ducks in a single innings — a proper spell of quack-making. First to go was John Thirkell, bowled by Kemp for his 1st duck of the season and a scarcely believable 47th of his career — still the club's all-time leader on 1 of 772, a three-time Duck of the Year (1952, '54 and '55) and a fixture of the Ducks on the Road, Homebody Duck and Lone Duck top tens. The old master, still setting the standard for not scoring. Roy Clarke followed, caught behind off Kemp for his 1st of the season and 26th career duck, good enough for 5th on the all-time list and a Duck of the Year winner back in 1959. Handily, his fall echoes down the years neatly — on this very day in 1952, John Thirkell made his own duck against Maidstone Trades, and here he was doing it again eleven years on, this time dragging company with him. That company was Bob Arnold, also bowled by Kemp, his 1st of 1963 and 40th career duck, 2nd on the all-time chart. Bob's honours board already carries Duck of the Year 1963 — bang up to date — plus a historic Ducks in a Row of four on the bounce. His board also lists "Quacking Together with John Thirkell", and with both men back in the pavilion for nought in the same innings, that pairing has never looked more current. 🏏 Sunday 28th — home to Maidstone AKCC A quieter harvest, but a historic one. B Norman, on debut, was bowled by William Dover for a golden entry into the Debutante Duck honours — the purest way to start a career. It stands as his 1st duck for 1963, and the record book has already filed him under One and Done for the season. Whatever comes next, this is one for the archive. Michael Chambers also fell, bowled by Eddie Page, his 4th career duck from 18 innings, 71st on the all-time list. Sunday's pair both land on a well-thumbed page in the archive — on this same calendar day in 1956, R Vincent made his own duck, his 1st for a career that ran to just one season. 📊 Week in Summary Five ducks, two matches, one very productive bowler in Ron Kemp, and Linton's newest member arriving in style with a debut nought. The 1st XI carried the entire weekend's misfortune — the 2nds, 3rds and Sunday sides escaped unscathed, for now. 🥇 Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard - B Norman — 1 innings, 1 duck, 100% - Bob Arnold — 1 innings, 1 duck, 100% - Michael Chambers — 1 innings, 1 duck, 100% - John Thirkell — 2 innings, 1 duck, 50% - Roy Clarke — 2 innings, 1 duck, 50% Early doors yet in the hunt for Duck of the Year 1963 — plenty of time for the chasing pack to catch Bob Arnold. 🍩 See you next round, Linton — the ducks are never far away. 0️⃣🏏

3 ducks
Week 22 · 22 Sep 1962 – 23 Sep 1962
The season's final furlongs and Linton Park's bowlers found the edge just often enough to keep the honours board ticking over. Three matches, three ducks, and not a golden one among them — a weekend of quietly professional failure. Saturday 22nd — 1st XI at Maidstone YMCA CC Jack Knowler fell for nought at number seven, bowled by E- Page. Only his second senior innings for the club, and he's already opened his OTHER account — a maiden career duck that lands him 265th of 769 all time. Week in brief Three matches, three ducks, no golden ducks, no repeat offenders — just tidy, one-per-match departures from Maidstone to the Married v Singles decider. 🦆 Duck Report — 1 & 2 September 1962

1 duck
Week 19 · 1 Sep 1962 – 2 Sep 1962
A quiet weekend on the poultry front — just the two fixtures and a single duck to show for it. Sometimes the hunting season goes like that. Even the finest game keepers have their off days. Saturday 1 September 1st XI v A. Trembeths (home) Coming in at ten, Richard Harris departed caught Bowey, bowled Tootle — a tidy dismissal for the scorebook, if not for Richard. It's his first duck of the season, but the 36th of a long and storied career spanning 174 innings, and it plants him at a genuinely eye-watering 3rd in the entire 767-strong all-time standings. This is not a man dabbling in the art of not scoring — this is a master craftsman. And in a rather splendid quirk of the calendar: on this very day back in 1934, Bert Buckoke also walked back for nought, against Charles Arkcoll of all people. Buckoke, who turned out for Linton Park between 1928 and 1953, finished his career on 12 ducks and a highly respectable 19th all-time, with back-to-back Duck of the Year honours in 1928 and 1950 to his name. Twenty-eight years apart, same fixture window, same fate — the club's ducks have a long memory. Sunday's fixture, mercifully or otherwise, passed off entirely duck-free — eleven batsmen apiece got off the mark, denying the honours board any further custom. Week in Summary Two matches, one duck. Slim pickings by Linton Park standards, but Richard Harris made it count, climbing to within a whisker of the all-time podium. Clarke still wears the 1959 Duck of the Year crown, and his "Quacking Together" pairing with Ames, usually a quiet historical footnote, was very much reactivated this week — the two of them walking off to the same bowler in the same over. It's the 2nd duck of Basil's season and the 12th of a career now running to 226 innings — enough to sit him a lofty 17th of 760 in the all-time table, the sort of consistency of a very particular kind that keeps a name near the top for all the wrong reasons. Rather splendidly, on this very day back in 1952, none other than club legend John Thirkell — he of 45 career ducks, three-time Duck of the Year and permanent resident of the Lone Duck and Homebody Duck top tens — was also walking back for nought against Marden CC, Kent. Some dates simply attract the zero. Down at number 6, Don Clayton became the innings' second casualty, bowled by H- Clancy. A tidier debut into the exclusive zero club than most: his first duck of the season and the first of his career, in only his 7th innings, landing him at 204th of 760 — a place of dubious distinction he now shares the calendar with, funnily enough, the very same John Thirkell fixture of 1952. Two Linton men, ten years and two dismissal methods apart, both nodding at 2nd June history. 📅 Week in Summary Two fixtures, two ducks, both delivered in the same innings by the same opposition — A.Trembeths clearly came prepared. The weekend's other match, elsewhere on the fixture list, proved a duck-free zone, batsmen keeping their heads determinedly above water. Triumph through adversity was thin on the ground this week, but the art of not scoring lives on regardless. Duck Hunting Season leaderboard 🥇 Basil Sears — 3 innings, 2 ducks (67%) 🥈 Michael Chambers — 1 innings, 1 duck (100%) 🥉 Percy Brattle — 1 innings, 1 duck (100%) 4. R Davison — 1 innings, 1 duck (100%) 5. Don Clayton — 4 innings, 1 duck (25%) Three names already on a flawless 100% this season — truly a poultry effort, in the finest sense. Basil leads the way on raw volume, but with the season young there's everything still to play for in the race for Duck of the Year. Next fixture beckons, and with it, no doubt, fresh additions to the honours board. Bat carefully out there. 0️⃣🦆

🦆 Duck News — 28-29 April 1962

4 ducks
Week 1 · 28 Apr 1962 – 29 Apr 1962
Two fixtures, four ducks, and the 1962 season's zero club already off to a flying — or rather grounded — start. Saturday 28th — Away to West Farleigh CC Basil Sears opened the innings and departed just as promptly, bowled by Ray Ford for his first duck of the new season. It's his 11th career nought from 224 innings, good (bad?) enough for 19th on the all-time list of 759. Neat bit of timing too — on this very day back in 1956, R Vincent suffered an identical fate against the very same West Farleigh CC. Some fixtures just breed ducks. Down at number 7, Percy Brattle followed him back, trapped lbw by Ron Kemp — his own season opener and 5th career duck from just 30 innings, sliding him into 55th spot all-time. He shares that same 1956-on-this-day West Farleigh coincidence with Basil. A chip off the old block, too — his relative Frank Brattle carries 15 career ducks of his own, so the family clearly knows the walk back well. Sunday 29th — Home to Maidstone AKCC John Ames, also opening, was bowled by Michael Chambers for his 26th career duck in 181 innings — a lofty 4th of 759 all-time. Ames arrives with a mantelpiece groaning under honours: Ducks in a Row for four on the spin, a place in the Homebody Duck top 10, Quacking Together billing with both Roy Clarke and Stan Wratten, and an exclusive Only Two Quacks arrangement with Alan Wilkes. A one-man social club of scorelessness. At number 6, Robert Wood was bowled by D Sadler for career duck number 18 from 119 innings, 8th of 759 all-time — and a proud old boy of the Debutante Duck club, having opened his account with a nought many innings ago. He now sits level on 18 with Gordon Fenner, who racked up the same tally across 1941–1962 and 143 innings. Week in Summary Four ducks, two matches, and the 1st XI cornering the entire market — top and middle order both doing their bit. West Farleigh claimed two openers-and-late-order pairs by lunchtime Saturday; Maidstone AKCC matched them exactly on Sunday. Consistency, of a very particular kind. 🏏 Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard 🏏 - Basil Sears — 1 inn, 1 duck (100%) - John Ames — 1 inn, 1 duck (100%) - Percy Brattle — 1 inn, 1 duck (100%) - Robert Wood — 2 inn, 1 duck (50%) Early days yet — plenty of season left for someone to break away from this perfect four-way tie at the top. At nine, Brian Relf was bowled by C- Smith without scoring — his 3rd of the season, 11th career, 18th of 754 all-time. A long-standing member of the Debutante Duck society from his very first innings, Brian shares Saturday's misfortune with the same Ernest Cruttenden of 1895. Monday 7th August — Bearsted CC (away) A two-innings friendly at Bearsted turned into a feeding frenzy — five noughts in one fixture. Opening up, John Ames was bowled by Mike Morton for his 2nd duck of the season (23rd career, 4th of 754 all-time) — then walked out again in the second innings and was caught George Lambell off Peter Longley for his 3rd of the season and 24th career duck. A genuine pair, both halves in the same match. Fittingly, his old honours-board accomplices Roy Clarke and Alan Wilkes — both immortalised alongside him for shared quacking down the years — were there to make it a proper reunion. Gordon Fenner obliged again at eleven, caught George Lambell off Mike Morton, his 3rd duck of the season and 18th career — and with Saturday still fresh in the memory, a pair spread neatly across the weekend. Roy Clarke (b Bryan Elswood) fell without scoring for his 2nd of the season, 22nd career, 5th of 754 all-time — solid work for a man who once carried the 1959 Duck of the Year title. His brother H Clarke sits on 3 career ducks of his own. Alan Wilkes (b Mike Morton) rounded things off with his 2nd of the season and 16th career, 10th of 754 all-time. All four of Monday's fallers share the same on-this-day parallel — back in 1909, C Stevens was doing exactly the same against the Royal West Kent Regiment CC, en route to the 1909 Duck of the Year gong. 📋 Week in Summary Seven ducks from two matches, with Monday's Bearsted friendly doing the heavy lifting — five for nought in one afternoon is precisely the team effort this club exists to celebrate. Two full pairs recorded too: Fenner's spread across the weekend, Ames' compressed into one glorious afternoon. 🥇 Duck Hunting Season leaderboard - Robert Murray — 20 innings, 4 ducks (20.0%) - Brian Relf — 5 innings, 3 ducks (60.0%) - Gordon Fenner — 11 innings, 3 ducks (27.27%) - John Ames — 16 innings, 3 ducks (18.75%) - John Crellin — 17 innings, 3 ducks (17.65%) Murray leads for now, but Relf, Fenner, Ames and Crellin are queuing up right behind him with plenty of season left to close the gap. 0️⃣ Next fixture, next chance for immortality — see you all next week for the inevitable additions to the book. 🦆

0 ducks

A quiet weekend at Linton Park, and not the good kind of quiet. Two matches came and went and not a single batsman offered himself up to the exclusive zero club. Two from two. A paid-up member of the Debutante Duck club since his very first knock also went scoreless, William now sits at 151 of 748 all-time and is yet to trouble a scorebook in senior colours. On this very day in 1950, D Simmons was likewise back in the shed without scoring, one of four ducks across a career that ran 1949 to 1953 — kindred spirits, eleven years apart. 🥇 Saturday 14th — v Halfway House Roger Mills had himself a day, claiming two ducks in the same innings. First to go was Eddie Lawrence, trapped lbw at three, his first duck of the season and sixth of a 28-innings career, moving him to 40th of 748 all-time. On this same date in 1955, William Blight also departed for nought against Gore Court, en route to 10 career ducks between 1953 and 1959. Then Mills struck again, this time bowling debutant Musgrave at nine for a golden entry into senior cricket. A duck on debut is never the start anyone wants, but it is precisely the start the Debutante Duck board exists to honour — and for now Musgrave's ledger reads a poultry one from one, top and tail of the same innings. Coincidentally, he too finds his name beside William Blight's 1955 effort on this calendar date. Last man Alan Wilkes then ran himself out for a third Halfway House duck, his fifteenth career nought from 57 innings and good enough for 10th of 748 all-time — rarefied company. Alan already shares the Only Two Quacks honour with both Bob Arnold and John Ames, so today's effort simply adds to an already distinguished portfolio of failure. Fittingly, the day's third parallel also lands on William Blight's 1955 duck — a busy anniversary for Gore Court ghosts. 📋 Week in Summary Four ducks, two matches, all 1st XI — Halfway House alone accounted for three, with Roger Mills doing the damage for two of them. A debut duck, a run-out, an lbw and a stumping: variety, at least, in the manner of departure. 🍩 Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard The season is young enough that the entire top five sit level on a single innings and a single duck apiece — a perfectly egalitarian 100% club, for now: - Musgrave — 1 inns, 1 duck, 100% - Alan Wilkes — 1 inns, 1 duck, 100% - D- Wright — 1 inns, 1 duck, 100% - Vic Pound — 1 inns, 1 duck, 100% - William Agate — 1 inns, 1 duck, 100% 🥎 Looking Ahead Early season form is always the most democratic — everyone's still got a perfect record of failure. Roll on the next fixture, where somebody is bound to spoil it. 0️⃣🦆

2 ducks

A rare feat to collect the full set before you've even opened your account. Fittingly, Wright shares that same 1956 echo — Sutton's second scalp of the day walking the very same historical path as Haylor. 📊 Week in Summary Two matches, two ducks, both from the same 1st XI innings and both administered by the same bowler — Sutton clearly fancied his chances against the home order. Both victims were also, remarkably, on senior debut, meaning Staplehurst's afternoon doubled as an involuntary induction ceremony for the Duck Club. A modest total, but a memorable one: not every week produces two brand new members in a single sitting. 🥇 Duck Hunting Season leaderboard 1. D- Wright — 1 innings, 1 duck (100%) 2. 0 ducks

It won't last. With the season stretching out ahead and more fixtures on the horizon, normal service — a nick behind, a plumb lbw, a golden duck for the ages — will surely resume shortly. 🦆 DUCK REPORT — 24–25 September 1960 🦆

8 ducks
Week 22 · 24 Sep 1960 – 25 Sep 1960
A blustery end-of-season weekend produced eight ducks across two fixtures, and the exclusive zero club is looking rather plump for it. Two truths were reaffirmed: the art of not scoring is alive and well at Linton Park, and nobody should let Ray Howard near a cricket ball if they value their stumps. Saturday 24th — 1st XI v A. Trembeths Frank Brattle departed to H- Clancy without troubling the scorers, his 4th duck of the season and 12th of an increasingly decorated career from 104 innings — good enough for 15th on the all-time list. A family trait, it seems: kinsman Percy Brattle already carries 4 career noughts of his own. On this very date in 1955, John Carter also strolled back for nought, against Town Malling CC, in what proved his only season in Linton colours. Sunday 25th — a full house against Linton Park CC Three Linton sides took the field, and the zero club signed up six new members for the day. Ray Howard led the way, bowled by John Ames for his 2nd duck of the season (8th career, 32nd all-time from 80 innings) — and then went and did the same to others. With the ball he claimed a treble of duck-scalps in the same innings, sending back Sean Carter, John Abnett and Derek Pantony all bowled. Poacher and gamekeeper on the same afternoon, and arguably better with the ball than the bat. Cliff Anscombe edged behind for his 3rd season and 10th career duck (22nd all-time, 33 innings), a paid-up member of the Debutante Duck club and a past (1957) Duck of the Year, still finding new ways to add to the collection. Sean Carter went one better — or worse — completing a pair: stumped off Len Conway's bowling for his 2nd duck of the season, then bowled by the rampaging Ray Howard for his 3rd, taking his career tally to 3 from just 6 innings (100th all-time). Two ducks, one date, no complaints. Len Conway, run out for his trouble, moved to 6 career ducks (44th all-time, 73 innings) and his 2nd of the season, himself a Debutante Duck alumnus of some vintage. John Abnett's was his 2nd of the season and 16th career duck from a mere 42 innings — a startling 7th on the all-time list — and sits comfortably alongside his own "Ducks in a Row" board entry. Derek Pantony's was his 5th of the season, a genuine title charge, and 6th career duck (39th all-time), the old 1947 Duck of the Year proving he's lost none of his touch for the art. History rhymed all afternoon: no fewer than six of Sunday's fallen discovered that on this exact date back in 1955, Frank Brattle — Saturday's own man of the moment — was himself out for nought against Linton Park CC. Some ghosts never leave the crease. 📊 Week in Summary 8 ducks, 2 matches, one treble of duck-taking, one pair, and Ray Howard doing more damage with ball than bat ever could. Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard - Pat Hardwick — 6 ducks / 37 inns (16%) - Richard Harris — 5 ducks / 11 inns (45%) - Derek Pantony — 5 ducks / 12 inns (42%) - Bob Arnold — 5 ducks / 19 inns (26%) - Robert Wood — 5 ducks / 34 inns (15%) 🍩 The season presses on, and so does the hunt for glory — or its rather more common opposite. Alan Wilkes rounded things off, Spanswick's third victim, his 3rd of the season and 14th career duck, joining Frank Sutton (1925–1949) on the same mark. Alan's own trophy cabinet includes "Only Two Quacks" pairings with both Bob Arnold and John Ames. Tuesday 26 July — Mote A (Away) A solitary entry at Mote A: Roy Clarke, bowled by Ashurst for his 3rd duck of the season and 19th career — rank 5 of 736, and a former Duck of the Year himself back in 1959. On this very day in 1959, none other than Tony Snell also departed against Folkestone CC — Linton's own "Runaway Duck" of 1958, a season memorable for yielding no runs whatsoever. Roy's sibling H Clarke also flies the family flag with 3 career ducks of his own. Week in Summary Eight ducks from three matches, with Bill Taylor and John Spanswick between them accounting for six of the eight — the bowlers rather outperforming Linton's top order this week. Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard 🏏 - 🥇 Bob Arnold — 12 inn, 4 ducks, 33% - 🥈 Robert Wood — 25 inn, 4 ducks, 16% - 🥉 Brian Relf — 4 inn, 3 ducks, 75% - Alan Wilkes — 6 inn, 3 ducks, 50% - Derek Pantony — 9 inn, 3 ducks, 33% Roll on the next fixture, when the exclusive zero club will no doubt be recruiting once again. 🍩0️⃣🦆

🦆 Duck News — 16th & 17th July 1960

4 ducks
Week 12 · 16 Jul 1960 – 17 Jul 1960
A short, sharp weekend for the exclusive zero club — every sighting crammed into one unfortunate innings at home to Rumwood CC on the Saturday, while Sunday's return fixture passed off entirely fowl-free. Saturday — 1st XI v Rumwood CC (home) The top order held until Gordon Fenner departed at four, bowled by J Carter, for his 1st duck of the summer and 15th of a genuinely distinguished LPCC career — good enough for 8th on the all-time list of 736, level with John --'s Taylor (1949–1958, 142 innings) and John Abnett (1954–1960). A name already familiar to the honours board through his brothers Joe (5 career ducks) and Maurice (1) — and spookily, on this very day in 1910, F S W Cornwallis also strolled back for nought against Maidstone CC. Carter clearly liked what he saw, because Bob Arnold followed at eight in identical fashion — his 4th duck of the season and 35th of his career, 2nd on the all-time chart of 736. Bob is paid-up in Ducks in a Row (4 consecutive), Only Two Quacks (with Alan Wilkes) and Quacking Together (with John Thirkell), and currently sits proudly atop this season's Duck Hunting standings on 4 from just 10 innings — a scarcely believable 40%. That same 1910 date claimed another victim too. Ricky Lusher, in at nine, edged behind to Carter's third — his 1st duck of the season and, remarkably, the very first blemish of his senior career after 10 clean-ish innings, ranking a relatively spotless 294th of 736. The 1910 echo held true for him as well. And to close out a thoroughly haunted afternoon, Brian Relf fell to R Galgey at ten for his 2nd duck of the season and 7th of his career, 30th on the all-time chart. Brian is a fully paid-up member of the Debutante Duck club from his very first LPCC innings years ago, carries the Retirement Duck and Quack-to-Quack honours from a past farewell, and shares Quacking Together status with Terry Whittaker — none of it news for today, but fine company on the board regardless. Week in Summary Four ducks from two matches, all four squeezed into the same Rumwood collapse, with Carter claiming three scalps in the same spell. Sunday's fixture, by contrast, was a vegan affair from start to finish. 🦆 Duck Report — 9th to 10th July 1960 🦆

0 ducks
Week 11 · 9 Jul 1960 – 10 Jul 1960
A quiet weekend on the poultry front, ducklers. Two fixtures went off across Saturday and Sunday and, remarkably, every single batsman who walked out for Linton Park found a way to trouble the scorers before departing. Not so much as a golden nought, not a single fresh entry for the honours board. The exclusive zero club held no inductions this week. 🍩 The ducks, it seems, took evasive action. Whether it was generous bowling, generous umpiring, or a rare outbreak of application at the crease, the art of not scoring went entirely unpractised. Even our most reliable operators found the middle of the bat. Frankly, some of the regulars below will be relieved — and others faintly disappointed not to have extended their tallies while the getting was good. Still, two matches is two matches, and the season is young yet. Nobody should get comfortable. 🏆 Duck Hunting Season leaderboard 🥇 Bob Arnold — 3 ducks in 9 innings (33.33%) 🥇 Derek Pantony — 3 ducks in 9 innings (33.33%) 🥇 Eddie Lawrence — 3 ducks in 9 innings (33.33%) - Terry Whittaker — 3 ducks in 10 innings (30.0%) - Robert Wood — 3 ducks in 20 innings (15.0%) A genuine three-way tie at the summit for Arnold, Pantony and Lawrence, all locked at 33% — a photo finish in the race nobody wants to win outright but everybody secretly eyes. Whittaker breathes down their necks with a touch more graft behind his total, while Wood holds his spot on volume alone, having ground out 20 innings for his trio of noughts. Triumph through adversity indeed, gentlemen — just not this week. 📅 Looking ahead A blank weekend for the Duck Club is a strange sort of anticlimax — like turning up to the ground and finding the wicket's been relaid. Rest assured it won't last. With the season's front-runners level at the top and plenty of willow still to be waved rashly at good-length deliveries, normal service will surely resume at the next fixture. 🦆 Duck Report — 2 & 3 July 1960

4 ducks
Week 10 · 2 Jul 1960 – 3 Jul 1960
Four fresh names added to the exclusive zero club this weekend, all courtesy of the 1st XI, who contrived not to trouble the scorers in either fixture. The art of not scoring, alive and thriving at Linton Park. 🏏 Saturday 2 July — v Charles Arkcoll The Debutante Duck honours board welcomes its newest member: W- Nash, playing his very first innings for the club, departed at number eight without scoring, caught by his own teammate Sean Carter off the bowling of Reg Waters. A debut to remember for all the wrong reasons — the ledger already has him down provisionally under One and Done and Retirement Duck, should this prove his only visit to the crease, though the selectors will no doubt want a second opinion first. On this very day in 1955, G Hill made his own duck against these same opponents, also on debut — some fixtures simply demand a sacrifice. Derek Pantony followed him back not long after, caught and bowled by the tireless Reg Waters for his 3rd duck of the season and 4th of an increasingly duck-heavy career, now sitting 58th of 736 on the all-time chart. A past Duck of the Year back in 1947, Derek continues to add to a fine and dubious legacy. He shares the very same on-this-day fate as G Hill, both ducking against Charles Arkcoll five years apart to the date. 🏏 Sunday 3 July — v Tovil Robert Murray was bowled by Brian Fridd for nought, his 1st duck of the season and 3rd of a 62-innings career, ranking 97th of 736 all time. On this day in 1955 the legendary John Ames — 21 career ducks, and a name on the Ducks in a Row and Homebody Duck honours boards — was busy adding to his own noble tally, albeit against different opposition. And spare a thought for Sean Carter, twenty-four hours after pouching the catch that did for Nash, who found himself making the same lonely walk back — caught by M- Patey off M- Bristow for his 1st career duck in just his 2nd innings, now 300th of 736 on the all-time list. He too joins the John Ames on-this-day club. Poetic justice, or just cricket. 📊 Week in Summary Four ducks 🍩, two matches, one thoroughly unfortunate 1st XI. Nash's maiden 0️⃣ and Carter's catch-then-duck double act were the tales of a weekend where the willow stayed conspicuously unblooded. 🥇 Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard 1. Bob Arnold — 8 inns, 3 ducks (37.5%) 2. Derek Pantony — 9 inns, 3 ducks (33.33%) 3. Eddie Lawrence — 9 inns, 3 ducks (33.33%) 4. Terry Whittaker — 10 inns, 3 ducks (30.0%) 5. Robert Wood — 19 inns, 3 ducks (15.79%) Pantony's Saturday effort keeps him right in that hunt. Next fixture awaits — the ducks, no doubt, are already limbering up. 🦆🏏

Four fixtures out this week, and the zero club recruited six new members between them — the Saturday clash at home to A.Trembeths doing the bulk of the damage. 1st XI v A.Trembeths (home, Sat 25th) A four-duck innings — the club practically fielded its own top order for the exclusive zero club. Triumph through adversity, truly. Hartridge, 1950, keeps him company again. Terry Whittaker rounded off the collapse at ten, bowled for his 3rd of the season and 6th career (rank 41), a paid-up member of Quacking Together alongside Brian Relf and the Retirement Duck honours from a past farewell. Hartridge's 1950 shadow lingers over this one too. Midweek XI v Benenden CC (away, Wed 29th) Eddie Lawrence departed bowled by D- Elliott for his 3rd duck of the season and 5th of his career, rank 44 of 732. Not quite king pair territory, but a proper double all the same. He too finds himself keeping Cruttenden's 1907 company. Robert Wood's Saturday-to-Wednesday pair was the tale of the week, and Pat Hardwick keeps his nose in front for Duck of the Year 1960. 🦆 LPCC Duck Club Bulletin — 18–19 June 1960 🦆

4 ducks
Week 8 · 18 Jun 1960 – 19 Jun 1960
Rumwood CC provided the hunting ground this weekend, with the 1st XI's trip away yielding a full quartet of noughts. A quiet weekend elsewhere, but Rumwood more than made up for it. 🏏 1st XI at Rumwood CC Batting at four, T- May fell b J- Carter without troubling the scorers — and it's a debut to remember for all the wrong reasons. His maiden senior innings ends in a duck, earning immediate and simultaneous membership of three honours boards: Debutante Duck, One and Done, and the Retirement Duck club (the last two, naturally, presumptive — nobody's writing his farewell speech just yet). On this very day back in 1949, club legend John Thirkell was doing exactly the same thing against Bowaters CC, en route to a colossal 44 career ducks and the No.1 spot in the all-time rankings. Good company to keep, even from the bottom of the ladder. At five, H Clarke was run out for nought — the fielding side doing the bowler's work for him. It's Clarke's 3rd career duck from 18 innings, sitting him at 84th all-time, and a paid-up member of the Debutante Duck club from his own first-baller some innings back. He's got form in the family too — sibling Roy Clarke carries a hearty 18 career ducks, so the nought clearly runs in the blood. Like May, Clarke shares this day in history with John Thirkell's 1949 vintage. Number seven Terry Whittaker was bowled by J- Carter, his 2nd of the season and 5th for his career — a tally that lands him at 48th all-time, level with the likes of Allan Peach (1903–1907) and Frank Wright, the latter a fellow member of the exclusive Quack-to-Quack club. Terry already shares Quacking Together honours with team-mate Brian Relf — and rather fittingly, Relf was next through the gate. Brian Relf, batting nine, was stumped off the same tireless J- Carter, his 1st duck of the season and 6th of his career, moving him to 34th on the all-time list. Brian's card is a crowded one — Debutante Duck, Quack-to-Quack, Quacking Together with Whittaker, and Retirement Duck all present and correct, a full house of dubious distinction. He now sits alongside D Sells (1943–1944), who also stopped the clock on six. Four wickets, one bowler, one stumping — J- Carter clearly fancied his chances against Linton Park this week, and the Duck Club is grateful for the service. 📊 Week in Summary Four ducks from two matches, all four falling in the same innings at Rumwood — a proper collective effort, and every single one of them credited to the same bowler. The art of not scoring was alive and well on the away trip, even if the rest of the fixture list stayed disappointingly fowl-free. 🥇 Duck Hunting Season leaderboard - Bob Arnold — 3 ducks in 8 innings (37.5%) - Alan Wilkes — 2 ducks in 3 innings (66.67%) - Eddie Lawrence — 2 ducks in 5 innings (40.0%) - Derek Pantony — 2 ducks in 6 innings (33.33%) - Terry Whittaker — 2 ducks in 8 innings (25.0%) Alan Wilkes lurking on a fearsome 66.67% strike rate should have the rest of the club nervous. Roll on next weekend — the ducks at Rumwood clearly enjoyed the company, so who's joining them next? 🍩

4 ducks

A quiet couple of days by Duck Club standards, but the exclusive zero club still found four new inductees at Headcorn and Halfway House. Robert Wood departed at number five for his 1st duck of the season, bowled by S Parnham, and now stands on 8 career ducks — 28th of 730 all time. A paid-up member of the Debutante Duck club from way back, though today's effort was a solo affair rather than a repeat performance. Poetically, on this very day in 1955, Bob Arnold also made a duck against Headcorn CC — Arnold went on to rack up 34 of the things (2nd of 730 all time), so Robert keeps distinguished company on the calendar if not yet on the leaderboard. Down at number ten, Tony Snell followed him back with a golden-tinged 1st duck of the season, caught Murrell bowled Ward. Tony now sits on a mighty 19 career ducks — 5th of 730 all time — a Duck of the Year winner in 1958 and holder of the "Runaway Duck" board for that same barren campaign. Fittingly, he shares his on-this-day company with the very same Bob Arnold, also felled by Headcorn on 11 June 1955. 🏏 Saturday/Sunday — Halfway House Away The 1st XI's trip to Halfway House on the 12th brought two more names to the party. John Abnett, in at nine, edged behind for his 1st duck of the season and moves to 15 career ducks — 9th of 730 all time. A quietly serious tally that puts him level on career ducks with John "--'s" Taylor, who racked up his 15 across 142 innings between 1949 and 1958. On this same date back in 1865, W Crittenden also made a duck, against 1st Innings Yalding United — the club's ducking traditions clearly run deep. But the standout of the weekend belongs to Derek Pantony, bowled by Roger Mills at number ten for his 2nd duck of the season, taking him to just 3 career ducks from a mere 7 innings — a frankly alarming 43% strike rate in the wrong direction. Derek is already a Duck of the Year alumnus from 1947, and tonight joins a long and distinguished queue on exactly 3 career ducks, including E Hayes (3 from just 3 innings — a perfect and terrible record) and Michael Fagg. Also on this day in 1865, W Crittenden made his duck against Yalding United — the calendar clearly has a taste for these things. 📊 Week in Summary Four ducks from two matches, all in the 1st XI, all away from home — Linton's top order clearly fancied giving the locals a show without troubling the scorers. No pairs, no golden family affairs, but Derek Pantony's second duck of the weekend deserves a nod for pure economy of effort. 🥇 Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard 1. Bob Arnold — 7 innings, 3 ducks (42.9%) 2. Alan Wilkes — 3 innings, 2 ducks (66.7%) 3. Eddie Lawrence — 5 innings, 2 ducks (40.0%) 4. Derek Pantony — 6 innings, 2 ducks (33.3%) 5. Frank Brattle — 10 innings, 2 ducks (20.0%) Alan Wilkes leads on strike rate but Bob Arnold holds the volume crown for now. All the damage confined to the 1st XI this week — the lower sides keeping their powder dry, for now.
